verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              पौरवेणाथ वयसा ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः। प्रीतियुक्तो नृपश्रेष्ठश्चरा विषयान्प्रियान्॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Having thus received the youth of Puru, Yayati the son of Nahusha, that best of kings, was exceedingly delighted. He again indulged in the pleasures of life.

verses.sanskrit: यथाकामं यथोत्साहं यथाकालं यथासुखम्। धर्माविरुद्धं राजेन्द्रो यथा‍ऽर्हति स एव हि॥२॥
verses.english: He enjoyed himself to the full extent of his desires and to the full limit of his powers, as much as he desired and as the seasons called forth. But, O king, he did nothing against the precepts of religion.

verses.sanskrit: देवानतर्पयद्यज्ञैः श्राद्धैस्तद्वित्पितॄनपि। दीनाननुग्रहैरिष्टैः कामैश्च द्विजसत्तमान्॥३॥
verses.english: He pleased the celestials, by performing sacrifices, the Pitris by Shraddhas, the poor by charities and the good Brahmana by fulfilling their desires.

verses.sanskrit: अतिथीनन्नपानैश्च विशश्च परिपालनैः। आनृशंस्येन शूद्रांश्च दस्यून्सन्निग्रहेण च॥४॥
verses.english: The guests by food and drink, the Vaishyas by protection, the Shudras by kindness and the robbers by proper punishments, Yayati pleased all classes of his subjects by ruling over them virtuously like Indra.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मेण च प्रजाः सर्वा यथावदनुरञ्जयन्। ययातिः पालयामास साक्षादिन्द्र इवापरः॥५॥
स राजा सिंहविक्रान्तो युवा विषयगोचरः। अविरोधेन धर्मस्य चचार सुखमुत्तमम्॥६॥
verses.english: That king was as powerful as the lion. He was young and enjoyed all the pleasures of life. He enjoyed unlimited happiness without violating the precepts of religion.

verses.sanskrit: स संप्राप्य शुभान्कामांस्तृप्तः खिन्नश्च पार्थिवः। कालं वर्षसहस्रान्तं सस्मार मनुजाधिपः॥७॥
verses.english: The king (Yayati) became exceedingly happy in thus being able to enjoy all the best objects of enjoyments. That king of men was only sorry (in remembering) that one thousand years would soon come to an end. That royal sage, learned in the mystery of time and possessed of great prowess, having obtained youth for one thousand years and watching proper Kalas and Kashthas. Sported with Vishvachi (Apsara), some time in the garden (of Indra) Nandana, sometimes in Aloka and sometimes on the summit of the Meru Mountain. That virtuous king then found that the fixed time (one thousand) years had come to an end. He then called Puru and addressed him thus.
verses.bhavadeepa: विषयाः दिव्यगन्धादयो गोचरे वशे यस्य सः विषयगोचरः ॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: परिसंख्याय कालज्ञः कलाः काष्ठाश्च वीर्यवान्। यौवनं प्राप्य राजर्षिः सहस्रपरिवत्सरान्॥८॥
विश्वाच्या सहितो रेमे व्यभ्राजन्नन्दने वने। अलक्तायां स कालं तु मेरुशृङ्गे तथोत्तरे॥९॥
verses.english: He enjoyed for a long time the sweet company of his two wives. He enjoyed with (Apsara) Vishvachi in the gardens of Chitraratha (Gandharva king.)
verses.bhavadeepa: परीति । सौरवर्षे हि प्रत्यब्दं पञ्चदिनानि पञ्चदशनाड्यस्त्रिंशत्पलानि एकत्रिंशदक्षराणिवर्धन्ते । सावनैः षष्ठयधिकशतत्रय दिनात्मकैर्वर्षैरायुर्गण्यतेऽतः कलाःकाष्टाश्च । 'अष्टादशनिमेषास्तु काष्ठास्त्रिंशत्तुताः कला, इत्युक्तरूपाः संख्यायेत्युक्तम् ॥८॥

verses.sanskrit: यदा स पश्यते कालं धर्मात्मा तं महीपतिः। पूर्णं मत्वा ततः कालं पूरुं पुत्रमुवाच ह॥१०॥
यथाकामं यथोत्साहं यथाकालमरिन्दम्। सेविता विषयाः पुत्र यौवनेन मया तव॥११॥
verses.english: O son, O chastiser of foes, I have enjoyed with your youth to the full extent of my desires and to the full limit of my powers and all according to their seasons.
verses.bhavadeepa: पश्यते सः कालं कालोऽपि तं ग्रसितुं पश्यतीत्याशयेन कर्मव्यतिहारे ‘तङ्’ ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit: न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति। हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते॥१२॥
verses.english: But desires never die. They are never satiated by indulgence. By indulgence they flame up like the sacrificial fire with ghee poured into it.

verses.sanskrit: यत्पृथिव्यां व्रीहियवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः। एकस्यापि न पर्याप्तं तस्मात्तृष्णां परित्यजेत्॥१३॥
verses.english: If one becomes the sole lord of all the earth with its paddy, oats, gems, beasts and women, still it will not be considered by him enough. Therefore, the thirst for enjoyment, should be abandoned.

verses.sanskrit: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः। योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तांतृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम्॥१४॥
verses.english: The thirst (of enjoyments), which is difficult to be cast off by the wicked, which does not fail even with falling life, is truly a fatal disease in man. To get rid of this thirst is real happiness.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्णं वर्षसहस्रं मे विषयासक्तचेतसः। तथाप्यनुदिनं तृष्णा ममैतेष्वभिजायते॥१५॥
verses.english: My mind was attached to the pleasures of life for full one thousand years. My thirst for them, however, without being abated, is daily being increased.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादेनामहं त्यक्त्वा ब्रह्मण्याधाय मानसम्। निर्द्वन्द्वो निर्ममो भूत्वा चरिष्यामि मृगैः सह॥१६॥
verses.english: Therefore, I shall get rid of it. I shall fix my mind on Brahma and becoming peaceful and having no attachment, I shall pass the rest of my days in the forest with the innocent deer.

verses.sanskrit: पूरो प्रीतोऽस्मि भद्रं ते गृहाणेदं स्वयौवनम्। राज्यं चेदं गृहाण त्वं त्वं हि मे प्रियकृत्सुतः॥१७॥
verses.english: O Puru, I am exceedingly pleased with you. Take (back) your own youth. Prosperity be to you. Receive my kingdom. You are my son who has done my favourite work.
verses.bhavadeepa: ब्रह्मज्ञानमेवात्यन्तिकतृप्तिहेतुर्न विषयभोग इत्याशयेनाह । तस्मादिति । एनां तृष्णां द्वन्द्वानि शीतोष्णमानापमानसुखदुःखादीनि तद्रहितो निर्द्वन्द्वः । द्वन्द्वकल्पकस्य मानसस्य ब्रह्मणि निधानात् अत एव निर्ममः अहङ्कारस्यैव ममतामूलस्य त्यागात् ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              प्रतिपेदे जरां राजा ययातिर्नाहुषस्तदा। यौवनं प्रतिपेदे च पूरुः स्वं पुनरात्मवान्॥१८॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Yayati, the son of Nahusha, then received back his own old age and his son Puru also received back his youth.

verses.sanskrit: अभिषेक्तुकामं नृपतिं पूरुं पुत्रं कनीयसम्। ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा वर्णा इदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥१९॥
verses.english: Yayati became desirous of installing his youngest son Puru on the throne. But the four orders of his subject with Brahmanas at their

verses.sanskrit: कथं शुक्रस्य नप्तारं देवयान्याः सुतं प्रभो। ज्येष्ठं यदुमतिक्रम्य राज्यं पूरोः प्रयच्छसि॥२०॥
verses.english: “O lord, how can you install Puru on the throne, passing over your eldest son Yadu, born of Devayani and grandson of Shukra?

verses.sanskrit: यदुर्ज्येष्ठस्तव सुतो जातस्तमनु तुर्वसुः। शर्मिष्ठायाः सुतो द्रुह्युस्ततोऽनुः पूरुरेव च॥२१॥
verses.english: Yadu is your eldest son, after him was Turvasu. Then Sharmishtha's son Druhyu, Anu and last Puru.

verses.sanskrit: कथं ज्येष्ठानतिक्रम्य कनीयान्राज्यमर्हति। एतत्संबोधयामस्त्वां धर्मं त्वं प्रतिपालय॥२२॥
verses.english: How it would be proper to pass over all the elders and install 1 the youngest? We represent this to you, act according to the precepts of religion.

verses.sanskrit:
ययातिरुवाच।
              ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा वर्णाः सर्वे शृण्वन्तु मे वचः। ज्येष्ठं प्रति यथा राज्यं न देयं मे कथंचन॥२३॥
verses.english: Yayati said : Hear all of you of the four orders of the caste with the Brahmanas at their head, why my kingdom should not be given to my eldest son.

verses.sanskrit: मम ज्येष्ठेन यदुना नियोगो नानुपालितः। प्रतिकूलः पितुर्यश्च न स पुत्रः सतां मतः॥२४॥
verses.english: My commands were disobeyed by my eldest son. The opinion of the wise men is that the son disobeys his father is no son at all.

verses.sanskrit: मातापित्रोर्वचनकृद्धितः पथ्यश्च यः सुतः। स पुत्रः पुत्रवद्यश्च वर्तते पितृमातृषु॥२५॥
verses.english: The son who obeys the commands of his father and mother, who is humble and a wellwisher of his parents and who loves them, is the best of sons.

verses.sanskrit: यदुनाऽहमवज्ञातस्तथा तुर्वसुनाऽपि च। द्रुह्युना चानुना चैव मय्यवज्ञ कृता भृशम्॥२६॥
verses.english: I have been slighted by Yadu and Turvasu; much have I been slighted by Druhyu and Anu.
verses.bhavadeepa: मातेति । अनौरसोऽपि यः पुत्रवद्वर्तते स एव पुत्रो नत्वन्यः ॥२५॥

verses.sanskrit: पूरुणा तु कृतं वाक्यं मानितं च विशेषतः। कनीयान्मम दायादो धृता येन जरा मम॥२७॥
verses.english: Only Puru obeyed my commands and much have I been honoured and respected by him. He accepted my old age and therefore, though he is the youngest, yet he should be made king.

verses.sanskrit: मम कामः स च कृतः पूरुणा मित्ररूपिणा। शुक्रेण च वरोदत्तः काव्येनोशनसा स्वयम्॥२८॥
verses.english: Puru is a great friend of mine and he did what was agreeable to me. And the son of Kavi, Ushanas, Shukra himself, granted me this boon. The son who would obey me would become the king and the lord of the earth. Therefore, I entreat you, let Puru be installed on the throne.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रो यस्त्वाऽनुवर्तेत स राजा पृथिवीपतिः। भवतोऽनुनयाम्येवं पूरू राज्येऽभिषिच्यताम्॥२९

प्रकृतय ऊचुः।
              यः पुत्रो गुणसंपन्नो मातापित्रोर्हितः सदा।	
              सर्वमर्हति कल्याणं कनीयानपि सत्तमः॥३०॥
verses.english: The people said : O king, it is true that, the son who is accomplished and who seeks the good of his parents, deserves all prosperity, though he is the youngest.

verses.sanskrit: अर्हः पूरुरिदं राज्यं यः सुतः प्रियकृत्तव। वरदानेन शुक्रस्य न शक्यं वक्तुमुत्तरम्॥३१॥
verses.english: Therefore, Puru, who has done good to you, deserve, to have the kingdom. As Shukra has granted this boon, we have no power to say anything.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              पौरजानपदैस्तुष्टैरित्युक्तो नाहुषस्तदा। अभ्यषिञ्चत्ततः पूरुं राज्ये स्वे सुतमात्मनः॥३२॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said: Having been thus addressed the contented people the son of Nahusha (Yayati) installed his son Puru on the throne.

verses.sanskrit: दत्त्वा च पूरवे राज्यं वनवासाय दीक्षितः। पुरात्स निर्ययौ राजा ब्राह्मणैस्तापसैः सह॥३३॥
verses.english: Bestowing the kingdom on Puru he resolved to live in the forest and he left his capital with Brahmanas and ascetics.

verses.sanskrit: यदोस्तु यादवा जातास्तुर्वसोर्यवनाः स्मृताः। द्रुह्योः सुतास्तु वै भोजा अनोस्तु म्लेच्छजातयः॥३४॥
verses.english: The son of Yadu are known as the Yadavas, those of Turvasu as the Yavanas, those of Druhyu as the Bhojas and those of Anu as the Mlecchas,

verses.sanskrit: पूरोस्तु पौरवो वंशो यत्र जातोऽसि पार्थिव। इदं वर्षसहस्राणि राज्यं कारयितुं वशी॥३५॥
verses.english: Those of Puru as the Pauravas, in which dynasty, O king, you are born to rule the country for one thousand years.
